title: Career Roadmap: Clinical Research Coordinator
summary: A Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC) helps organise and manage clinical research studies involving human participants. Working with principal investigators, doctors, research nurses, sponsors, and ethics committees, the coordinator supports study visits, participant communication, documentation, data collection, and compliance with approved research procedures.

blocks.text: A Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC) helps organise and manage clinical research studies involving human participants. Working with principal investigators, doctors, research nurses, sponsors, and ethics committees, the coordinator supports study visits, participant communication, documentation, data collection, and compliance with approved research procedures.

A B.Sc. in a relevant life-science or health-science discipline can provide a useful foundation, but eligibility depends on the employer, study type, and exact degree. A degree described as “physiotherapy-related basic sciences” may not automatically meet every CRC vacancy's requirements, so check the eligibility criteria carefully.
Recommended degree background
B.Sc. in an eligible health science, life science, biomedical science, clinical research, or related discipline. Confirm acceptance of the specific qualification with each employer.
Core focus
Clinical trial coordination, participant scheduling, study documentation, research ethics, protocol compliance, data quality, and regulatory recordkeeping.
Potential workplaces
Hospitals, academic medical centres, clinical research sites, contract research organisations (CROs), research institutes, and pharmaceutical or biotechnology companies.

items.text: Coordinate participant appointments, study visits, and follow-up schedules.
Support the informed-consent process using approved documents and trained supervision.
Organise study files, source documents, essential records, and version-controlled paperwork.
Help collect and enter study data accurately into approved research systems.
Track protocol requirements, visit windows, and missing information.
Communicate with investigators, participants, laboratories, sponsors, and research teams.
Support ethics committee submissions and maintenance of study documentation.
Prepare for monitoring visits, audits, and inspections.
Report protocol deviations, safety concerns, and adverse events through the required procedures.
Protect participant confidentiality and follow approved data-handling practices.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: A CRC does not independently diagnose conditions, change trial treatment, or make clinical decisions outside their professional authority. Medical care and study-related clinical decisions remain with appropriately qualified investigators and healthcare professionals.
Year 1 — Biomedical foundations

items.text: Study human anatomy, physiology, cell biology, and basic biochemistry.
Learn introductory research methods and medical terminology.
Practise reading scientific abstracts and research papers.
Understand research ethics, privacy, and participant rights.
Strengthen written English and spreadsheet skills.

blocks.text: Year 2 — Research methods and data

items.text: Learn study designs, sampling, descriptive statistics, and basic epidemiology.
Understand clinical outcomes, inclusion and exclusion criteria, and study protocols.
Practise data entry, data validation, and structured recordkeeping.
Study informed consent, confidentiality, and ethics committee functions.
Explore Excel and introductory clinical research terminology.

blocks.text: Year 3 — Clinical research operations

items.text: Learn Good Clinical Practice (GCP) principles and protocol compliance.
Practise creating study visit schedules, participant logs, and document checklists.
Understand adverse event reporting workflows and protocol deviation documentation.
Explore electronic data capture (EDC) and clinical trial management systems (CTMS).
Seek supervised exposure to a hospital research department or clinical research site.

blocks.text: Final-year focus — Job readiness

items.text: Complete a research-methods project or supervised research placement.
Prepare a mock study file and participant visit tracker using fictional data.
Learn document version control, audit trails, and data-quality checks.
Practise explaining a research protocol and identifying missing documentation.
Apply for eligible clinical research assistant, study coordinator trainee, or research support roles.

blocks.text: For a three-year degree, combine the final-year activities with Year 3.

Clinical research in India is governed by applicable regulations, ethics oversight, and Good Clinical Practice requirements. The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) publishes relevant clinical-trial rules and guidance.

blocks.label: Key concept
blocks.text: Clinical research requires accurate, traceable records. Never fabricate, backdate, or silently alter research information. Corrections and reporting must follow the study's approved procedures.
Use fictional scenarios or approved training datasets. These projects can demonstrate your readiness for research support work without involving real patient information.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Mock clinical study file

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Learn how clinical study documentation is organised.

items.text: Create a fictional study overview and protocol summary.
Prepare a document index and version-control log.
Draft a visit schedule and study task checklist.
Identify missing or inconsistent documents in a mock scenario.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A sample study-file index and document-control report.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Participant visit tracker

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Practise scheduling and tracking study visits.

items.text: Build a fictional participant register using unique study IDs.
Create visit windows, appointment status, and follow-up reminders.
Add checks for missing fields and overdue tasks.
Create a summary of completed and pending visits.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: Excel or Google Sheets. Deliverable: A functional study-visit tracker using fictional data.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Clinical research data-quality exercise

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Demonstrate careful data review.

items.text: Use a synthetic dataset with deliberately missing or inconsistent values.
Identify missing fields, duplicate records, and out-of-range values.
Maintain a discrepancy log and correction-status column.
Summarise data-quality issues without inventing missing information.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A data-quality report and discrepancy tracker.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Protocol compliance case study

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Understand how coordinators document and escalate study issues.

items.text: Write a fictional scenario involving a missed study visit or incomplete form.
Identify which protocol requirement is relevant.
Draft a factual issue record and escalation note.
Explain why safety concerns must be handled through the study's approved process.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A case study demonstrating documentation, escalation, and compliance awareness.
Do not use actual patient records in a personal portfolio. Use synthetic data and label all mock documents clearly as educational exercises.

blocks.text: A postgraduate qualification is not always necessary for an entry-level CRC position. First check whether your exact bachelor's degree is accepted by the employers you intend to target.
Entry level — Research Assistant / CRC Trainee
Support scheduling, documentation, study files, and supervised data collection.
Developing professional — Clinical Research Coordinator
Coordinate study activities, monitor visit schedules, and maintain accurate research records.
Experienced — Senior CRC / Lead Study Coordinator
Coordinate more complex studies, mentor colleagues, and support monitoring and audit readiness.
Advanced — Clinical Trial Manager / Research Operations Manager
Oversee study delivery, resources, timelines, quality, and cross-functional coordination.

Alternative pathways include clinical data management, pharmacovigilance, regulatory affairs, clinical trial monitoring, and research project management. Each has its own eligibility and experience requirements.

blocks.label: Electronic data capture (EDC)
blocks.text: entering and validating study data in controlled systems.

blocks.label: Electronic trial master files (eTMF)
blocks.text: maintaining structured, traceable study documentation.

blocks.label: Remote and hybrid trials
blocks.text: coordinating appropriate remote visits and digital study processes.

blocks.label: Wearables and digital endpoints
blocks.text: supporting collection of certain health-related measurements under approved protocols.

blocks.label: AI-assisted research workflows
blocks.text: supporting document organisation and data review while preserving human oversight.

blocks.label: Risk-based quality management
blocks.text: prioritising study processes and data that matter most to participant safety and study reliability.
Technology does not remove the need for participant protection, accurate records, protocol compliance, and appropriate human oversight.

Recommended target profile

By graduation, aim to become a research-ready candidate who understands clinical study procedures, maintains accurate documentation, handles data responsibly, and communicates effectively with a research team.
Your target profile should include:

items.text: A bachelor's degree accepted by your target employer.
Foundational knowledge of clinical research and GCP.
Strong documentation, Excel, and data-quality skills.
A portfolio of fictional study-coordination exercises.
Supervised research exposure, where available.
A clear understanding of ethics, confidentiality, and escalation procedures.

blocks.text: This preparation can help you target Clinical Research Assistant, CRC Trainee, Research Project Assistant, and eligible Junior Clinical Research Coordinator opportunities. The first step is to confirm that your specific undergraduate qualification satisfies the entry requirements of the employers you want to approach.
